prerequisites: Basic knowledge of sequential programs, with fundamental concepts for establishing variable types, execution flow control elements, program editing.
Reading level English is advisable for technical materials.

learning_outcomes.text: Students should know how to apply acquired knowledge and problem-solving skills in new or unfamiliar environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their field of study.
Students should possess learning skills that allow them to continue studying in a largely self-directed or autonomous way.
To project, calculate and design products, processes, facilities and plants.
To carry out research, development and innovation in products, processes and methods.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity and critical reasoning.
Ability to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering, both orally and in writing, and to all types of audiences.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Ability to design and project automated production systems and advanced process control.
Ability for the management of Research, Development and Technological Innovation.

Completion, presentation and defense, once all Master's credits have been obtained, of an original exercise performed individually before a university tribunal, consisting of a comprehensive Industrial Engineering project of a professional nature, in which the competencies acquired in the Master's are synthesized.
Know and apply programming fundamentals, data structures, algorithms, and interprocess communication to software development for robotic systems.
Use software development tools (integrated development environment, version control) appropriate to the framework of robotic systems.
Use scientific software libraries for information processing.
Know the ROS framework and be able to develop applications within it.
Know and use robot environment simulation tools.
Present and orally defend the completed project.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to C++ programming: Functions, input/output, control statements, pointers, namespaces, modules. Integrated development environments.
Tools for the development and design of computer systems: Test-Driven Development (TDD). Use of version control tools (git), collaborative work.
Object-oriented programming: classes, objects, inheritance. Definition and management of abstract data types (stacks, queues, trees, graphs, etc.).
Interprocess communications: handling of POSIX IPC calls via PyPi. Management of message queues, semaphores, and shared memory.
Use of specific libraries for robot handling and modeling: Use of ROS for simulation and evaluation of common robotics concepts.
teaching_methods: Laboratory practice / field / computer lab / language lab

assessment_methods.method: Completion of practicals and active attendance

assessment_rules: For the ordinary assessment, an individual project will be assigned, parts of which will be completed during laboratory practical classes and finalized through non-contact work. Students may be required to orally defend this work if it is deemed not to meet minimum quality and originality requirements; this project accounts for 80% of the grade, with a minimum passing score of 5 out of 10. The remaining 20% comes from laboratory practicals. In extraordinary assessments, students can choose between a project, which can account for 100% of the grade with a minimum passing score of 5 out of 10, or a written exam, which can account for up to 70% of the grade, with a minimum passing score of 7 out of 10. The same criteria apply for differentiated assessment.
